messages:
ops-bot: [ALERT] ALB target deregistered: targetId=i-0f3a2b7c, targetGroup=tg-edge-prod, reason=unhealthy (5 failed checks)

michael: seeing this alert too. any clue why /health is 404 from the pod? app is healthy in k8s.

jia: pulling logs now. quick note: ALB health checks hit NodePort -> kube-proxy -> pod, and ours has an Envoy sidecar that expects Host header 'app.service.internal' not IP. ALB sends host as node IP by default.

samir: that could explain a 404 from Envoy virtual_host mismatch. do we have host header override in the TG?

kevin: checked target group config — health check path = /health, protocol = HTTP, but Host header not set. AWS console doesn't show host override for our TG (classic case).

jia: log snippet from envoy access log: 
```
"GET /health HTTP/1.1" 404 - "-" "10.0.42.11:30845" x-forwarded-for:10.0.1.23
reason: no_route for virtual host '10.0.42.11'
```

michael: so ALB -> node IP host header -> envoy returns 404 -> ALB counts fail -> deregisters target. Intermittent because sometimes ALB health check hits pod directly?

samir: might be worse — we also saw spikes in SNAT ephemeral ports earlier which caused some checks to timeout/503 around the same window. two failure modes colliding.

kevin: commands I ran: `kubectl get pods -o wide -n edge` shows pods Running, readiness true. `ss -n sport sport` shows established ports ok; but `sudo conntrack -L | grep 10.0.1.23 | wc -l` peaked at 13000 during the window.

jia: TL;DR: Envoy virtual host mismatch is primary for 404s. SNAT port pressure probably caused extra timeouts which sped up deregistration.

michael: short-term fix? we can't change app immediately.

jia: options: 1) set TG health check host header to `app.service.internal` (preferred) — ALB supports overriding Host for HTTP checks via target group attribute; 2) add a lightweight local health endpoint on host network that responds to IP host header (nginx on node) and point TG to instance target type with externalTrafficPolicy=Local; 3) adjust Envoy vhost to accept node-IP host header (ugly).

samir: for the SNAT issue, we should also ramp up NAT port pool or enable node-local SNAT (e.g., kube-proxy/iptables MASQUERADE tuning) and open a follow-up.

kevin: I can flip the TG health-check host override to `app.service.internal` for one small ASG first (canary) — that's quick and reversible.

michael: do it. annotate the change and monitor. if healthy counts stabilize, roll to others.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: changing target group attribute tg-edge-prod.healthcheck_host -> 'app.service.internal' (canary) by kevin at 2026-03-18T14:12:10Z

kevin: changed on canary ASG. watching metrics.

jia: also creating ticket INFRA-4382 to track SNAT port exhaustion and add node-local egress or increase ephemeral port range.

samir: note for postmortem: healthcheck host header mismatch with service mesh sidecar + SNAT port pressure multiplying failures => faster ALB deregistration. add playbook step to check envoy access log for 'no_route' when debugging 404 health checks.

michael: nice catch. thanks team. :thumbsup:

kevin: update after 2m: canary nodes stayed registered, health checks passed 10/10 for 3 intervals. rolling to remaining ASGs now.

ops-bot: [INFO] target group tg-edge-prod: targets back to healthy after update (rolling).

michael: leaving ticket with next actions: (1) TG host override as default for all edge TGs; (2) INFRA-4382 for SNAT follow-up; (3) add a short runbook entry.

jia: I'll draft runbook blurb and link the envoy log grep.

kevin: PR for TG update in infra-aws repo is up: https://git.internal/infra-aws/pulls/412

samir: good. close the loop once SNAT work is scheduled.

michael: agreed, closing thread once INFRA-4382 is triaged.
